regions.summary: Han River uplands around Yunyang, Yunxi and Baihe, between Shiyan and the Shaanxi border.

candidates.name: Yunyang
candidates.meaning: Yun (the old Yun county, 郧乡) plus yang, the sunny side; the Ming prefecture (1476) of the whole Han-river highland was named Yunyang.
candidates.fit: Yun district (now Yunyang district) holds 44% of the region's people with 97% of its own; Yunxi (17%) was cut from Yun in 1476 and, like Fang, Zhushan and Zhuxi, belonged to the Ming Yunyang prefecture.
candidates.recognisability: Current district name (Yunyang since 2014); Shiyan is also called 古称郧阳 on zh-wiki; 929 hits with 湖北.

regions.notes: Yunxi (17%) and Danjiangkou (13%) are smaller; Danjiang is already a neighbour's name.

regions.summary: Shiyan's two urban districts, Zhangwan and Maojian (3.4M city, built around the Dongfeng car works).

candidates.name: Shiyan
candidates.meaning: "Ten weirs": Ming-era dams built on local streams to irrigate fields, which gave the town its name.
candidates.fit: Zhangwan (54%) and Maojian (46%) are the whole of Shiyan's urban core; it is the city's central region.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city.
candidates.source_note: 十堰作为地理名称来由…筑起十个堰

regions.summary: Han River plain and Wudang foothills: Gucheng, Laohekou and the Wudang mountain area of Danjiangkou.

candidates.name: Wudang
candidates.meaning: Wudang Mountain, the Daoist holy mountain; the name is traditionally explained as only the god Xuanwu being able to match (当) it.
candidates.fit: The mountain lies in Danjiangkou, and the Wudangshan special zone (4% of the region's people, 91% of the zone) is inside; Danjiangkou holds 26% of the people, Gucheng 46% and Laohekou 28%. A landscape name for the heart of the area, not the whole.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 761 hits with 湖北, top ones about this mountain; World Heritage site.
candidates.source_note: 位於湖北省西北部丹江口市境內，武当山旅游经济特区即依此山而定名

candidates.name: Gucheng
candidates.meaning: Gu city: after the ancient state of Gu (谷国), whose ruler's mound and city lay on Gu Mountain northwest of the town.
candidates.fit: Gucheng county holds 46% of the region's people (82% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Laohekou
candidates.meaning: "Old river mouth": the mouth of the old Han channel, a 1937 market-town name replacing the older Guanghua.
candidates.fit: 28% of the region's people; a city of 470k.
candidates.recognisability: Smaller share than Gucheng, and a trade-town name; Wudang covers the area's identity better.

regions.summary: Plains north and west of the Xiangyang city core: Xiangzhou district, parts of Zaoyang and Fancheng.

candidates.name: Xiangzhou
candidates.meaning: Xiang prefecture: the Sui-Song prefecture (583-1118) seated at Xiangyang, and the name of today's district around it.
candidates.fit: Xiangzhou district holds 51% of the region's people (70% of the district); the other 20% each are Zaoyang and Fancheng.
candidates.recognisability: Current district name (襄阳区 until 2010).

regions.notes: Not the central Xiangyang region (see 8). Xiangzhou (襄州) and Xiangyang (襄阳) are different characters.

regions.summary: The Du River highland: Zhushan, Fang and Zhuxi counties, the south of Shiyan prefecture.

candidates.name: Zhushan
candidates.meaning: Bamboo mountain; in the Three Kingdoms the area was called Shangyong.
candidates.fit: Largest of the three counties (37% of the region's people, 99.9% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Fang
candidates.meaning: "Room": one explanation is that the ring of mountains forms the walls and the sky the roof. The county was Fangling in Qin-Tang times.
candidates.fit: Fang county holds 31% of the people (88% of the county); the Tang prefecture Fangzhou was seated here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county name; one character, so Fangxian in English.

candidates.name: Duhe
candidates.meaning: Du River, the biggest tributary of the Han; the character means to block or dam, origin of the name not given.
candidates.fit: The river rises in Zhuxi and flows through Zhushan and Fang before joining the Han, so it runs through all three counties.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 177 hits with 湖北, mostly reservoirs and counties of this area; known mainly locally.
candidates.source_note: 汉江最大支流堵河位于该县境内 (竹山县)

candidates.name: Zhuxi
candidates.meaning: Bamboo stream.
candidates.fit: 28% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Smallest of the three counties and Zhushan carries the same bamboo name.

regions.notes: Shangyong (上庸, ancient Yong state and Three Kingdoms commandery at Zhushan) was checked: 41 hits with 湖北, no article of its own, so left out.

regions.summary: The dense old centre of Fancheng, the north bank of the Han opposite old Xiangyang.

candidates.name: Fancheng
candidates.meaning: Fan city: the walled town on the Han's north bank, historically paired with Xiang city across the river as the twin cities Xiang-Fan.
candidates.fit: Fancheng district holds 80% of the region's people (62% of the district); it is the commercial half of Xiangyang.
candidates.recognisability: Current district name and half of the old name Xiangfan.

regions.notes: Xiangyang goes to region 8 because it holds the walled old city (Xiangcheng, Pangong, Longzhong) and the simplemaps city point. Region 6 is the densest core, though, so Anita may prefer Xiangyang here and Fancheng for 8; both fit.

regions.summary: Zaoyang city and the Sui county uplands between the Tongbai and Dahong mountains.

candidates.name: Zaoyang
candidates.meaning: Jujube sun: from Zaoyang village; the county took its name from it in the Sui dynasty (601).
candidates.fit: Zaoyang holds 65% of the region's people (73% of the city); it is a 1M-person county-level city, home of the Han emperor Liu Xiu's ancestral area.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

candidates.name: Sui
candidates.meaning: The old state of Sui (Zeng), whose Marquis Yi tomb is at Suizhou.
candidates.fit: 35% of the region's people (54% of Sui county).
candidates.recognisability: Name belongs to Suizhou city, which sits outside this region; the Sui county seat and Leigudun tomb are elsewhere.

regions.summary: Old Xiangyang: Xiangcheng, Yuliangzhou island, Dongjin and Yicheng on the Han's south bank.

candidates.name: Xiangyang
candidates.meaning: Xiang plus yang (sunny side); the county has carried the name since 202 BC and the city was Xiangfan until 2010.
candidates.fit: Holds the walled old city (Xiangcheng district: Pangong, Tanxi and Longzhong streets) and the simplemaps point for the 5.3M prefecture; Xiangcheng is 31% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city, centre of the central region.

candidates.name: Yicheng
candidates.meaning: "Suitable city": renamed from Yan (鄢), the Chu capital region, in 192 BC.
candidates.fit: 40% of the region's people (73% of Yicheng).
candidates.recognisability: The central region takes the city name; Yicheng is the largest single unit though and would be the fallback.

regions.notes: Yicheng's old name Yan (鄢, Chu capital Yingdu region) was not checked for hits.

regions.summary: Jing Mountain country: Nanzhang and Baokang, the Han's southwest highlands.

candidates.name: Nanzhang
candidates.meaning: South of the Zhang River, named in the Sui dynasty (598).
candidates.fit: Nanzhang holds 49% of the region's people (99.7% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Jingshan
candidates.meaning: Jing Mountain (Mount Jing), the 150 km range where the Chu people began; the Ju, Zhang and Man rivers rise here.
candidates.fit: The range covers Nanzhang and Baokang, which are 73% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 148 hits with 湖北, top ones about this range and early Chu. Shares pinyin with Jingshan county (京山, different characters).
candidates.source_note: 荆山位于中国湖北省西部,长约150公里；沮河、漳河以及蛮河发源于此山

candidates.name: Baokang
candidates.meaning: "Protect and keep well": linked to a Song garrison name and read as wishing the people peace and comfort.
candidates.fit: 24% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Smaller than Nanzhang, and a keep-the-people-safe style name.

regions.summary: The Three Gorges highlands: Zigui, rural Yiling, Yuan'an, Xingshan and most of Shennongjia.

candidates.name: Zigui
candidates.meaning: By tradition from Qu Yuan's elder sister coming home (归) to urge him; the poet's birthplace and an old Kui state.
candidates.fit: Zigui holds 29% of the region's people (97% of the county); the Tang-Qing prefecture Guizhou (归州) was seated here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Sanxia
candidates.meaning: The Three Gorges of the Yangtze: Qutang, Wu and Xiling; the Xiling Gorge, longest of the three, and the Three Gorges Dam lie in this region.
candidates.fit: Xiling Gorge runs between Zigui and Yiling, and the dam site Sandouping is in rural Yiling.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 245 hits with 湖北, all about this place or its dam.
candidates.source_note: 西陵峡 ... 西起湖北省秭归县香溪口，东至宜昌市夷陵區南津关

candidates.name: Yiling
candidates.meaning: "Yi mound": the Chu kings' burial mounds; the old name of Yichang.
candidates.fit: 34% of the region's people (63% of the rural district).
candidates.recognisability: Old Yiling's seats lay in the Yichang city region (11), so the name fits there better.

regions.summary: Yichang city: Xiling, Wujiagang and the Xiaoxita part of Yiling (4M prefecture).

candidates.name: Yichang
candidates.meaning: "Suited to prosper": the name from a Jin-era county, applied to the Qing prefecture seat in 1735.
candidates.fit: Xiling (62%) and Wujiagang (24%) hold the urban core; it is the city's central region.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city; simplemaps shows a 4M point called Xiaoxita here.

candidates.name: Xiling
candidates.meaning: "West mound": after the Xiling Gorge and mountain.
candidates.fit: 62% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: The central region takes the city name.

regions.summary: Badong and Jianshi, the Wu Gorge side of Enshi prefecture.

candidates.name: Badong
candidates.meaning: "East of Ba": the Ba lands lay to the west in Chongqing and eastern Sichuan.
candidates.fit: Badong holds 39% of the region's people (99% of the county); the Wu Gorge's eastern end is here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Jianshi
candidates.meaning: "Beginning of founding": a county since 265; the sources do not explain the name.
candidates.fit: Jianshi holds 37% of the region's people (99.9% of the county); Tang Yezhou was seated here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Wuxia
candidates.meaning: The Wu Gorge, middle of the Three Gorges, from Wushan in Chongqing to Guandukou in Badong.
candidates.fit: Its eastern 45 km lies in Badong.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; named in all Three Gorges coverage.
candidates.source_note: 巫峡西起重庆市巫山县大宁河口，东至湖北省巴东县官渡口

regions.summary: Dangyang and Zhijiang on the Yangtze's northern bank at the edge of the Jianghan plain.

candidates.name: Dangyang
candidates.meaning: Qin-era county name (278 BC); the name is literally "facing the sun". Site of Changban slope and Mai city.
candidates.fit: Dangyang holds 40% of the region's people (75% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

candidates.name: Zhijiang
candidates.meaning: "Branch river": the Yangtze divides like the limbs of a tree here.
candidates.fit: Zhijiang holds 44% of the region's people (74% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

regions.notes: Dangyang and Zhijiang are of similar size; no landscape name stands for both.

regions.summary: Qing River lower valley: Changyang, Yidu, Dianjun and Wufeng, south of the Yangtze.

candidates.name: Qingjiang
candidates.meaning: "Pure river": the Qing River, a right bank tributary of the Yangtze; its valley is the homeland of Lord Lin of the Ba.
candidates.fit: Runs through Changyang and meets the Yangtze at Yidu, the two largest units here (57%).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 822 hits with 湖北, top ones about this valley; English article Qing River.
candidates.source_note: The Qing River (Chinese: 清江) lit. 'Pure River'

candidates.name: Changyang
candidates.meaning: The county of Changyang Tujia Autonomous County; the name's origin is not given in the sources. Site of the Palaeolithic "Changyang Man" (185,000 years).
candidates.fit: Holds 31% of the region's people (99.5% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county name.

candidates.name: Yidu
candidates.meaning: "Fit to be a capital": named by Liu Bei in 210 for a commandery.
candidates.fit: Yidu holds 26% of the region's people (88% of the city); the Qing River joins the Yangtze here.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

regions.notes: Qingjiang is used here and not in 16 (Enshi), though the river also rises near there.

regions.summary: Lichuan and the Chongqing county of Shizhu, southwest of the Qiyao mountains.

candidates.name: Lichuan
candidates.meaning: Literally "beneficial river"; county since 1735, the sources do not explain the name. Home of the folk song Longchuan diao.
candidates.fit: Lichuan holds 59% of the region's people (77% of the city).
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city.

candidates.name: Shizhu
candidates.meaning: Literally "stone pillar"; Shizhu Tujia Autonomous County in Chongqing, once a Tujia chieftaincy (Shizhu xuanfusi, 1375-1620).
candidates.fit: Shizhu holds 40% of the region's people (82% of the county).
candidates.recognisability: Current county name; old Qing spelling 石砫.

regions.summary: Enshi city and the counties of Xuan'en and Xianfeng, the seat of Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture.

candidates.name: Shizhou
candidates.meaning: Shi prefecture: from the ancient Shi state; the Tang-Song prefecture (618-1389) seated at Enshi, later the Shizhou garrison.
candidates.fit: Seat at Enshi city (77% of the region's people, 82% of the city); the Tang prefecture covered the area from Jianshi west.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 581 hits with 湖北, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 施州...治沙渠县（隋改清江县，今湖北恩施市）

candidates.name: Enshi
candidates.meaning: "Bestow grace": coined in 1728 when the Qing abolished the native chieftaincies, from Shi plus the emperor's favour (恩).
candidates.fit: Enshi city holds 77% of the region's people; it is the prefecture seat.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city and prefecture name.

regions.notes: Enshi's name comes from the Qing taking over from the Tujia and Miao chieftains; Shizhou is older and neutral, so ranked first. Xuan'en (14%) and Xianfeng (9%) have similar grace-style names (宣恩 'proclaim grace', 咸丰 an emperor's reign name).
